# HarborBuddy

HarborBuddy is a noncommercial source-available Go service that keeps containers on a standalone Docker Engine current through image-ID comparison, transactional replacement, readiness checks, and rollback.

Last substantive update: 2026-08-08
Maintainer: MikeO7 — https://github.com/MikeO7
Canonical website: https://mikeo7.github.io/HarborBuddy/
Source repository: https://github.com/MikeO7/HarborBuddy
License: PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0; commercial use is not permitted by the current license.

## Intended use

- Run continuously on a standalone Docker Engine host.
- Check for new images on an interval or at a configured daily time.
- Recreate eligible containers only when the pulled image ID differs from the running image ID.
- Verify a replacement before removing the temporary backup.

## Update and rollback behavior

- HarborBuddy pulls the exact configured image reference and compares immutable image IDs.
- It re-inspects a container before changing it to detect concurrent changes.
- The prior container is renamed as a temporary backup while the replacement is created and started.
- A health check is used when available; otherwise HarborBuddy waits through a configurable stabilization period.
- Creation, startup, or readiness failure removes the failed replacement and restores the old container's name and networks.
- Docker Swarm tasks, auto-remove containers, and containers sharing another container's network namespace are skipped.

## Control and maintenance

- Containers are managed by default unless excluded by configuration or the `com.harborbuddy.autoupdate=false` label.
- Image allow and deny patterns are supported; deny rules take precedence.
- Dry-run mode pulls images and updates the local image cache, but does not stop, recreate, rename, or remove containers and does not remove or prune any cleanup resource.
- Cleanup defaults to dangling images older than 24 hours.
- `HARBORBUDDY_CLEANUP_ALL=true` additionally enables stopped-container, unused-network, unused-volume, build-cache, and unused-tagged-image cleanup.
- Each aggressive cleanup category has an independent environment switch and defaults to off.
- System or in-use resources and resources with unknown age or usage are protected. Volume cleanup can remove application data after its final container reference is gone.
- Logs use stable event names and correlated cycle IDs, with severity-correct update, cleanup, transaction, rollback, and self-update outcomes.
- Startup records the effective non-secret configuration. Cleanup records concise per-resource summaries; routine skips move to debug so warnings and failures remain visible.
- Logs can use console text or production-recommended JSON, with optional rotating files.

## Automatic self-update

- Automatic self-update is enabled by default and can be disabled independently.
- A short-lived helper replaces the HarborBuddy daemon after the daemon exits.
- The helper retains the old daemon as a backup until the new daemon passes startup readiness.
- `HARBORBUDDY_CONTAINER_NAME` should identify the daemon's stable container name in Compose deployments.

## Security boundary

- HarborBuddy requires read/write Docker API access to pull images and create, stop, rename, start, and remove containers.
- Docker daemon access is equivalent to host-level administrative access.
- Run only one active HarborBuddy controller per Docker daemon.
- Remote Docker endpoints must be secured with Docker's standard TLS environment variables.
